title: Best Sightseeing Pair
statement: Spot `i` along a road has attractiveness `values[i]`, and two spots `i` and `j` are `j - i` apart. For indices `i < j`, the pair scores `values[i] + values[j] + i - j`, which is the two spots' values added together minus how far apart they are. Return the largest score that any pair of spots can reach.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every pair is O(n²). Split the score into two parts: `(values[i] + i) + (values[j] - j)`. The first part depends only on the left spot and the second only on the right spot. So when the scan reaches `j`, the best partner is simply the largest `values[i] + i` seen so far, which one running maximum can track.

## Approach

1. Set `bestLeft = values[0] + 0`, the best left part using spot `0`, and `best` to minus infinity.
2. For each `j` from `1` to the end:
   - Pair `j` with the best earlier spot: `bestLeft + values[j] - j`, and keep the maximum in `best`.
   - Then let `j` become a candidate left spot: `bestLeft = max(bestLeft, values[j] + j)`.
3. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`values = [8, 1, 5, 2, 6]`, `bestLeft = 8`.

- `j = 1`: score `8 + 1 - 1 = 8`, `best = 8`; `bestLeft` stays `8`.
- `j = 2`: score `8 + 5 - 2 = 11`, `best = 11`; `5 + 2 = 7`, so `bestLeft` stays `8`.
- `j = 3`: score `8 + 2 - 3 = 7`; `bestLeft` stays `8`.
- `j = 4`: score `8 + 6 - 4 = 10`; `bestLeft` becomes `10`, but no spot follows.

The answer is `11` (spots `0` and `2`).

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over `values`.
- Space: O(1): two running numbers.

## Pitfalls

- Score `j` before adding it to `bestLeft`, or a spot would pair with itself.
- The left part gains `+ i` and the right part loses `- j`; mixing up the signs picks the wrong partner.
- The best pair is not always the two largest values: a big gap can cost more than it gains.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bestLeft` | largest `values[i] + i` over spots before `j` |
| `best` | highest pair score found so far |
| `j` | index of the right spot of the pair |

narration.2: Spot 0 is the only possible left spot so far; its left part is values[0] + 0.
narration.3: No pair has been scored yet.
narration.4: Treat every later spot as the right end of a pair.
narration.5: Pair j with the best earlier spot; its score is bestLeft + values[j] - j.
narration.6: Now j can serve as a left spot for later pairs, worth values[j] + j.
narration.8: best holds the largest score over all pairs.
